title: Imaging of Biological Tissues by Desorption Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry
protocol: Store flash-frozen whole tissue in -80°C freezer until ready for sectioning.
Allow the tissue sample to reach the temperature of the cryomicrotome (30 min).
Set the blade and sample temperature to -30°C.
Handle the specimen with tweezers, cut the front or back of the brain as needed.
Apply approximately 0.5 ml Optimal Cutting Temperature Compound to the chuck in the center.
Hold the sample in place in OCT using tweezers until it solidifies.
Mount the chuck in the sample holder once OCT is completely frozen.
Section tissues at a thickness within the range of 12-18 μm as desired.
Thaw-mount each sectioned tissue by lightly touching a room-temperature microscope glass slide over the section.
Mount two sections per slide for imaging optimization and analysis.
Store slides in -80°C freezer until ready for analysis if not used immediately.
Transfer slide from freezer to vacuum desiccator when ready for analysis.
Allow 15-20 minutes for the sample to thaw.
Turn on the syringe pump with acetonitrile containing 1% acetic acid as DESI solvent at a flow rate of 5 μl/min.
Apply 3,600 V high voltage power supply connected to the ion source.
Mount the slide on the motion stage.
Begin optimization and MS analysis.
Proceed with DESI source optimization after tuning the mass spectrometer for the appropriate mass range and analytes of interest.
Ensure the DESI source is not touching the glass slide or directed at any part of the tissue section initially.
Position the tip 3 mm from the sample surface and 5 mm from the MS capillary inlet.
Set the probe angle to 55° with respect to the sample surface.
Extend the inner capillary ~1 mm beyond the outer capillary.
Adjust the stage height so that the MS capillary hovers over the sample surface; the capillary should be <1 mm from the surface, as close as possible without touching.
Align the DESI probe in the x dimension with respect to the MS capillary inlet so that they are directly in line.
Adjust the y and z positions of the DESI source for optimal sensitivity using an extra tissue section.
Move the sample underneath the spray head to ensure fresh sample analysis during optimization.
Use the thalamus region of the brain for a relatively consistent chemical composition area.
Alternatively, mark the glass slide with red Sharpie away from the sample for MS response comparison.
Set the y separation between source tip and capillary inlet to approximately 4 mm.
Set the z separation between the tip and sample surface to approximately 1.5 mm.
Adjust the distance the inner capillary extrudes from the outer capillary for maximum sensitivity.
Set the high voltage to OFF while adjusting the capillaries.
Ensure the heating element around the transfer capillary is set to 100 °C to improve sensitivity.
Re-adjust variables as necessary to maintain optimal source-sample-inlet geometry.
Program the LabView VI or equivalent control software for desired imaging conditions.
Set the stage scan speed to 80 μm/sec.
Set the line spacing between rows to 200 μm.
When using the Omni Spray source, set the scan speed to 100-200 μm/sec.
Set the line spacing of 200 μm for the Omni Spray source.
Give directory path and file name for position and time files to be recorded during images within the LabView VI.
Calculate the total time required for imaging.
Input the time-per-line and number of lines necessary for given imaging dimensions into the mass spectrometer software.
Set spectral scan speed to 1 spectrum/sec.
Acquire data in PROFILE mode.
Ensure m/z range is appropriate for the species of interest.
Set acquisition time to match total image time given by LabView.
Position the spray impact spot in the top-left of the area to be imaged.
Begin acquisition of MS data and stage motion simultaneously.
Return mass spectrometer to STANDBY mode upon conclusion of data acquisition.
Turn off high voltage of DESI source.
Turn off nitrogen gas.
Turn off syringe pump.
Convert acquired data to centroided data using DataManager in MassCenter (Tools → Convert Acquistion Data to Centroid).
Export data in .cdf format from MassCenter using Ctrl+Shift+E followed by Tools → Export.
Upload raw .cdf mass spectral data and the two text files, position and time, to the OmniSpect website.
